about.heading: Self-taught, and building things that hold up.

paragraphs.text: I'm a self-taught full-stack developer from Chattogram. I began programming in 2025 and have since shipped a booking platform, a billing backend and a fitness platform.

What I enjoy most is the moment a hard problem finally makes sense. I try to build the parts users never see but always depend on: role-based access, payments, scheduled jobs, and graceful handling of retries and dropped connections.

In 2026 I completed the FlyRank AI Internship Program in the Backend AI Engineering track. Each of my three approved capstones ships with a design document, a build log and recorded evidence of its checks, along with a plain list of what it does not do.
Away from the keyboard, you'll find me with a book, any genre, or playing football.

projects.title: CarePoint
projects.summary: Doctor appointment platform where patients book real, conflict-free time slots and pay online, with tools for doctors, clinics and admins.
projects.problem: Booking a doctor usually means guessing which times are actually open, then paying separately, with no guarantee the slot has not been taken by someone else. Clinics and doctors, meanwhile, manage schedules, approvals and revenue across disconnected tools. CarePoint brings booking, payment and clinic operations into one platform for patients, doctors, clinic admins and super admins.
projects.approach: A Next.js client and a separate Express 5 REST API backed by PostgreSQL. Slots are computed on read from each doctor's weekly rules, leave days and existing bookings. A slot is held while the patient pays through Stripe Checkout, and four roles (patient, doctor, clinic admin, super admin) each get their own protected flows with ownership checked on every record.

keyDecisions.text: Let the database arbitrate double bookings with a partial unique index on (doctorId, slotStart) for active statuses, instead of row locking, so a new code path cannot forget the check. A test fires two simultaneous bookings for one slot and asserts exactly one succeeds.

Made payment confirmation independent of a single webhook. The Stripe webhook, a status-page sync and a 10-minute reconciliation sweep all use the same conditional update, so they are safe to run in any order or twice.
Made refunds refund-first and idempotent, using a Stripe idempotency key and updating the database only after Stripe succeeds, so an appointment can never be cancelled without returning the money.
Enforced authorization in the query itself (owner in the where clause), read roles from the database on every request, and shaped responses with select so private fields never leave the server.
Stored all times in UTC and interpreted them in the clinic's time zone, so a late-night slot never lands on the wrong date.

projects.outcome: Two simultaneous bookings for one slot are tested to produce exactly one winner, backed by a database-level unique index. Patients can pick a slot, pay and manage appointments, while doctors, clinic admins and super admins run schedules, approvals and reports through separate, protected flows. The server is covered by a test suite that runs against a real PostgreSQL database, including simultaneous booking, cross-user access, webhook ordering and refund failure cases, with CI running lint, build and tests on every push.

whatsNext.text: Always-on hosting or an external scheduler so reminder and payment-sweep jobs do not depend on a free-tier instance staying awake.
Emails for clinic and doctor approval decisions, and a way for rejected applicants to reapply.
End-to-end tests of the booking flow, plus structured logging and error tracking.

projects.title: Brawnix
projects.summary: Role-based gym and fitness class platform for members, trainers and admins.
projects.problem: Traditional gyms manage class discovery, booking, payment, and community engagement manually or through disconnected tools. Brawnix digitizes all of that into a single ecosystem for members, trainers, and administrators.
projects.approach: Three tier role based access control with isolated dashboards for Member, Trainer, and Admin. Stripe powered payments built directly into the class booking flow. A community forum with nested comment threads. A real time analytics dashboard for admins.

keyDecisions.text: Designed the three tier RBAC system with protected routes enforced via JWT verification on every API request, keeping each role's dashboard fully isolated.
Integrated Stripe into the booking flow while keeping checkout smooth and reliable, rather than bolting payment on as an afterthought.
Implemented server side pagination, search, and category filtering directly with MongoDB queries so the platform stays fast as data grows.

projects.outcome: The result is a working platform where three distinct user types, members, trainers, and admins, operate through separate, protected flows on one shared codebase.

whatsNext.text: A live class scheduling calendar with recurring session support.
Push notifications for class approvals and trainer responses.
An expanded analytics dashboard with revenue and retention insights.

projects.title: Thirsty for Knowledge
projects.summary: Bilingual minimalist blog where readers vote on what gets written next.
projects.problem: Most blogs are one-directional: an author writes, readers consume, and there's no real channel for readers to shape what comes next. Thirsty for Knowledge was built to close that gap for research-driven, long-form writing.
projects.approach: Admins publish long-form articles through a rich text editor, and readers engage through likes, threaded comments, and shares. A separate topic request board lets readers pitch ideas and upvote or downvote existing ones, giving the author a ranked signal for what to write next. Google OAuth via BetterAuth handles authentication with role-based access separating admin and reader permissions.

keyDecisions.text: Denormalized author name and image directly onto comment and topic request documents at creation time, after discovering BetterAuth's user collection isn't a registered Mongoose model and can't be `.populate()`d.

Wrote a small custom sanitization middleware after `express-mongo-sanitize` turned out to be incompatible with Express 5's read-only `req.query`, avoiding a third-party dependency for a problem solvable in a few lines.

Added a per-post `language` field with a client-side `<html lang>` switcher instead of pulling in a full i18n framework, since the site serves genuinely bilingual (Bengali/English) content post-by-post rather than a fully translated UI.
Configured cross-domain cookies (`sameSite: none`, `secure: true`) to fix OAuth session handling once the frontend and backend moved to separate production domains.

projects.outcome: A fully deployed, production-ready blog platform with content moderation tools, a voting-driven topic pipeline, and SEO fundamentals (structured data, sitemap, dynamic per-post metadata) in place from day one.

whatsNext.text: Real-time comment and vote updates with Socket.io.
AI-generated summaries for longer research articles.
An admin analytics dashboard tracking post performance and engagement trends.

projects.title: Healync
projects.summary: Doctor appointment booking for patients and verified medical specialists.
projects.problem: Booking a doctor's appointment usually still means a phone call or a manual hospital visit. Healync replaces that with a digital first flow that connects patients to verified specialists.
projects.approach: Patients browse verified specialists across multiple fields, book through a secure role protected flow, and manage their schedule in real time. An on demand Medical Companion service, automated email reminders via Nodemailer and node cron, and curated daily health tips round out the experience.

keyDecisions.text: Built a real time appointment dashboard so patients can view, update, or cancel bookings instantly without page reloads.
Folded the on demand Medical Companion request directly into the booking pipeline to keep the flow intuitive.
Automated email reminders with Nodemailer and scheduled cron jobs to proactively reduce no shows.

projects.outcome: A working booking platform that replaces manual scheduling with a self service, role protected flow between patients and specialists.

whatsNext.text: In app chat or video consultation for remote appointments.
SMS based reminders alongside the existing email system.
A dedicated admin and doctor dashboard for managing schedules, patient records, and companion assignments.
